title: Match Employee Codes with _ Wildcard
description:
Write a query to find employees whose `employee_code` matches the pattern `'EMP-_0_'` — meaning it starts with `EMP-`, followed by any single character, then `0`, then any single character. Return `id`, `name`, and `employee_code`.

**Table: employees**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| id | INT |
| name | VARCHAR |
| employee_code | VARCHAR |
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INT, name VARCHAR, employee_code VARCHAR); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1, 'Alice', 'EMP-101'), (2, 'Bob', 'EMP-201'), (3, 'Carol', 'CTR-101'), (4, 'Diana', 'EMP-301'), (5, 'Evan', 'MNG-101'), (6, 'Frank', 'EMP-401'), (7, 'Grace', 'CTR-201');
solution_sql: SELECT id, name, employee_code FROM employees WHERE employee_code LIKE 'EMP-_0_'

test_cases.description: Returns 4 employees with codes matching EMP-_0_ pattern (EMP-101, EMP-201, EMP-301, EMP-401)

hints: The `_` wildcard matches exactly **one** character, unlike `%` which matches any number.
`'EMP-_0_'` matches EMP- then any single char, then the digit 0, then any single char — so EMP-101, EMP-201, EMP-301, EMP-401 all match.
explanation: Each `_` in the pattern matches exactly one character. `'EMP-_0_'` matches 7-character codes starting with `EMP-` where the 6th character is `0`. All four EMP codes (101, 201, 301, 401) satisfy this.
